title: PulseFund: one-PDA-per-wallet SOL crowdfunding with an admin-only withdraw
summary: Each wallet opens one campaign account at ["CROWDFUND", wallet]. Anyone can donate SOL straight into that account, and only the campaign's admin can take it back out, never below the rent-exempt floor.
what: PulseFund is the smallest useful crowdfunding program: four instructions and one account type. `create` makes a 9,000-byte Campaign PDA at `["CROWDFUND", your wallet]` holding the name, description, links, category, a target and two running totals. `donate` moves SOL from the donor into **that same account** with a System Program transfer and adds to `amount_donated`. `withdraw` lets the admin pull lamports out by editing balances directly (the program owns the account), refusing anything that would dip below the rent-exempt minimum. `get_campaign` is an admin-only check that changes nothing. There are no deadlines, no refunds, and the target is only a number on the card.
app_note: The fork's own Next.js app exported as static pages with this devnet program ID; the only changes are basePath, unoptimized images and removing an unused example API route. **Goal Amount is in lamports** (1 SOL = `1000000000`). The app has **no withdraw screen**, and **Contribute always donates 0.2 SOL to your own campaign** (Exercise 1). Script: [tests/devnet/pulsefund-sol.mjs](https://github.com/Blockchains/sol-college/blob/main/tests/devnet/pulsefund-sol.mjs).

try_steps.do: Open [the app](/dapps/pulsefund-sol/) and connect Phantom on **devnet** with about 0.3 devnet SOL. Press **Create Campaign** and fill in Project Name, Description, Project Url, Category and **Goal Amount** `1000000000` (that's 1 SOL in lamports). Press **Publish Campaign**.
try_steps.see: One `create` transaction. Your wallet pays the rent for a 9,000-byte account, which was 0.04637024 SOL in our run. The account lives at `["CROWDFUND", your wallet]`, so a second Publish from the same wallet fails with "account … already in use".

try_steps.see: Your card shows something like **Raised $0 of $60475904** and **Remaining Days 30**. These numbers are wrong: the card prints the low 26 bits of the lamport value (1,000,000,000 mod 2²⁶ = 60,475,904), and the 30 days is hard-coded (Exercise 2). The list comes from `getProgramAccounts`, so it shows every campaign.

diagram:
admin wallet ─ create(name, description, target, urls, category) ─▶ Campaign PDA ["CROWDFUND", admin]   (9,000 bytes, rent paid by admin)
                                                                     admin, strings, target_amount, amount_donated, amount_withdrawn
any wallet  ─ donate(amount) ─▶ System transfer: donor ──amount──▶ Campaign PDA      amount_donated += amount
admin       ─ withdraw(amount) ─▶ if signer ≠ admin → IncorrectProgramId
                                  if lamports − rent_minimum < amount → InsufficientFunds
                                  Campaign.lamports −= amount; admin.lamports += amount; amount_withdrawn += amount
admin       ─ get_campaign() ─▶ admin check only (no state change)
reads       ─ getProgramAccounts(program) + fetch each Campaign (the home page)
accounts: Admin, name, description, target_amount (lamports), project/progress/image URLs, category, amount_donated, amount_withdrawn. The donated SOL is held **in this account's own lamports**

instructions.name: `create`: one campaign per wallet
steps: `init` with `seeds = [b"CROWDFUND", user]` makes the address depend only on the creator, so each wallet can have exactly one campaign. A second `create` fails at the System Program's `Allocate` ("already in use"), as our script recorded.

`space = 9000` is fixed. The creator pays rent for all 9,000 bytes up front (0.04637024 SOL in our run), and the strings are unbounded: if they add up to more than about 9,000 bytes, Anchor can't serialize the account and `create` fails (we read this from the code; it wasn't tested).
The handler copies the arguments in, zeroes both totals and records `admin = user`.

instructions.name: `donate`: SOL goes into the campaign account itself
steps: `campaign: Account<Campaign>` makes Anchor check the account is owned by this program and has the Campaign discriminator. A PDA that was never created fails with **AccountNotInitialized**.

The program builds `system_instruction::transfer(donor → campaign, amount)` and `invoke`s it. The donor's signature carries over into the CPI, and any account may *receive* lamports, including one owned by a program.

Then `amount_donated += amount` (the workspace builds with `overflow-checks = true`). Anyone can also send SOL to the PDA with a plain transfer. That SOL bypasses the counter but can still be withdrawn, because withdraw looks at lamports, not `amount_donated`.

instructions.name: `withdraw`: admin only, rent floor protected
steps: The accounts carry no `has_one`. The handler compares `campaign.admin` with the signer itself and returns the generic **IncorrectProgramId** for a stranger (our script's wallet B).

`rent_balance = Rent::minimum_balance(data_len)`, and the check `lamports − rent_balance < amount` → **InsufficientFunds**. With 0.02 SOL donated, asking for 0.03 failed and 0.015 succeeded; the account was left at 0.05137024 SOL (rent + 0.005), which matches the log.

There's no CPI here. Because the program **owns** the campaign account, it can lower its lamports directly (`try_borrow_mut_lamports() -= amount`) and raise the admin's, as long as the transaction's total doesn't change. System `transfer` can't be used *from* a program-owned account with data.

instructions.name: `get_campaign`: a check, not a read
steps: It only verifies that the signer is the admin (B got **IncorrectProgramId**) and returns. Calling it costs a transaction fee, and the app never calls it.
Real reads don't need an instruction: the home page fetches the accounts over RPC.

innovation.title: the campaign account is the vault
innovation.text: There is no separate escrow or vault PDA. The Campaign account's own lamports hold the donations: deposits come in through a System Program CPI, and withdrawals leave by direct lamport edits, which only the owning program may make. Rent-exemption is the one safety floor, so the account can never be drained to the point of being garbage-collected.
more: The trade-off: `amount_donated` is only bookkeeping. The real balance is `lamports − rent`, and that's what `withdraw` checks.
Nothing here enforces the *crowdfunding* rules: no deadline, no all-or-nothing target, no refund, and the admin can withdraw at any time. Those are Exercises 3 and 4.

frontend.title: Publish Campaign: PDA from your wallet
steps: It derives `["CROWDFUND", wallet]` with `findProgramAddress` and calls `program.rpc.create(...)` with the seven form fields.
`new BN(formState.targetAmount)` passes the number as typed, so the Goal Amount field is in **lamports**. Errors only go to the console.

frontend.title: Contribute: always your own campaign
steps: The card's PDA comes from `provider.wallet.publicKey`, the **connected** wallet, not the campaign shown on the card (the card isn't even given its pubkey). So every Contribute button funds the viewer's own campaign.
The amount is fixed at `0.2 * LAMPORTS_PER_SOL`.

frontend.title: Home: listing and amounts
steps: `getProgramAccounts(programId)` then `fetch` for each, on every load.
`targetAmount.words[0]` reads the first 26-bit limb of a BN, not the value. That's why 1 SOL shows as 60475904; `toNumber() / 1e9` would show 1.
`remainingDays: 30` and the "3 Active Campaigns" title are placeholders.

exercises.title: Make Contribute fund the card's campaign
steps: In `home/index.tsx`, pass `pubkey` through `convertToCampaign` into each card.
In `CampaignCard.tsx`, use that pubkey as `campaign` instead of deriving it from the connected wallet, and add an amount input in SOL.
exercises.expect: Wallet 2 pressing Contribute on wallet 1's card sends a `donate` whose campaign account is wallet 1's PDA, and wallet 1's raised amount goes up. This is what our script's B → A donation (czso1Hs3…) does at the program level.

exercises.title: Show real amounts
steps: Replace `.words[0]` with `.toNumber() / LAMPORTS_PER_SOL` (or `toString()` for safety) and label it SOL.
Accept Goal Amount in SOL on the form and multiply by 10⁹ before `new BN`.
exercises.expect: A 1 SOL goal shows **0 / 1 SOL**, not $0 of $60475904; after one Contribute it shows **0.2 / 1 SOL**, not $65782272.

exercises.title: Add a withdraw screen
steps: On the home page, if the connected wallet has a campaign, show its `lamports − rent` and a Withdraw button.
Call `program.rpc.withdraw(new BN(lamports), { accounts: { campaign, user } })`.
exercises.expect: Withdrawing everything above rent from your campaign works, as our script's 0.2 SOL withdrawal (34P4TJH1…) did. One lamport more gives InsufficientFunds.

exercises.title: Real crowdfunding rules
steps: Add `deadline: i64` to Campaign (and to `create`), and a `Donation` PDA `["donation", campaign, donor]` that records each donor's total.
`withdraw`: require `Clock.unix_timestamp ≥ deadline` and `amount_donated ≥ target_amount`.
Add `refund`: after the deadline, if the target was missed, pay the donor back their recorded amount and close their Donation PDA.
exercises.expect: Before the deadline the admin's withdraw fails. After a missed target, each donor gets exactly what they gave and the admin gets nothing.

exercises.title: Proper errors, size and close
steps: Replace the manual admin checks with `has_one = admin @ CrowdfundError::NotAdmin` and define custom errors instead of `IncorrectProgramId`/`InsufficientFunds`.
Add `#[max_len]` to the strings with `InitSpace` instead of `space = 9000`, and add a `close` instruction (`close = admin`) once the funds are withdrawn.
exercises.expect: B's withdraw fails with NotAdmin. A campaign with short strings costs well under the 0.04637024 SOL rent our run paid, and closing it returns the rent to the admin.

not_covered: Create and Contribute were clicked through in the app. Donating to another wallet's campaign, the withdrawals and every rejected case were run by script (run 1 was aborted by an RPC 503 outage; all results come from run 2). Not exercised: over-long strings in create (the 9,000-byte limit), and plain transfers that bypass donate.
